script: Sorry, I am just a typical woman. A long time ago, I worked as a receptionist at a law firm, where I took and transferred calls, greeted guests, and led them to the correct briefing rooms. It was my first gig after moving to town, so I was still figuring out the streets. But here's the thing—one call changed everything. The phone rang. A man's voice, thick with irritation, already screaming "what do you know about directions?" before I even asked how I could help him. I said I didn't know that town, but I could look it up. He cut me off and screamed into my ear, "Typical stupid woman, can't even tell directions!" and hung up. I thought, "Wow, rude much?" but I just shrugged it off. But here's the thing—this wasn't the first time I'd been on the receiving end of a bad attitude. Twenty minutes later, another guy storms in, same annoyed tone, demanding directions to the interview room.
